notes: Interpretation calls on items that were not scored: (1) The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation and Mr. Dell's United Nations Foundation 'Global Advocate for Entrepreneurship' title are personal or family activities of the CEO, not company activities, so they were not credited. (2) Dell Technologies Capital invests in early-stage companies, but the filing frames it as strategic venture investment to complement Dell's own portfolio, not as a program addressing founders' barriers; it was treated as at most own innovation or serving, not enabling. (3) Supplier 'skills building in areas such as forced labor and health and safety' is compliance-oriented supply-chain assurance, so it was not credited as external education; it would not change the Community score of 2 in any case. (4) The facilitated third-party financing for channel partners' working capital and the DFS financing ($11.9 billion originations) are ordinary customer and partner financing, so they count as serving only. (5) Traps excluded: 'foundation' used as a metaphor (several times in Item 1 and Item 7), 'AI model training', 'design' in the engineering sense, patent and software 'licensing', and 'innovative/innovation'. (6) The filing describes headcount reductions and limited external hiring in Fiscal 2026, but it does not say any development or ERG program was discontinued. (7) The targeted Item 7 excerpts contained no qualifying activity; they matched only on 'foundation' used as a metaphor.
